full_judgment:
3. In writ petition No. 8362 of 2009 and writ petition No. 7948 of 2009 Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner Md Azam-e-Sadat calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the initiation of Criminal Proceedings of Motijheel Police Station Case No. 79 and 77 dated 28-12-2006 respectively pursuant to lodging First Information Report with the Motijheel Police Station under sections 420/467/468/471/511/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Annexure-B) against the petitioner in violation of the provisions of section 32(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 now pending before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. Background leading to issuance of the Rules, in short, is that the informant respondent No. 3, Assistant Director, Anti-Corruption Commission lodged FIR with the Motijheel Police Station giving rise to Motijheel Police Station Case No. 77 and 79 both dated 28-12-2006 under section 420/667/468/471/511/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of the Corruption Act, 1947 against the petitioner and others. 

 5. In writ petition No. 8362 of 2009 the FIR case has been summarized in paragraph 8 of the petition. It is stated that the petitioner joined Internal Container Depot (ICD) at Kamalapur on 6-4-2003 and worked there till 18-12-2005 when he was promoted as Additional Commissioner of Customs and was posted. to a new place. It has been further stated that the allegation against the petitioner is that he has committed offence, that took place long after he relinquished his service on 18-12-2005, relating to evasion of customs duties and other charges amounting to Taka 43,64,187.03 at the behest of the importer Kaisarul Haque Robin who made a false declaration of importing 4200 glass Temblor in place of Perfume, Cigarette lighter, Cosmetics and photo film imported vide LC No.026806010128 dated 4-6-2006 covered by CRF No. BDH- 20067145-2C dated 17-7-2006 for which the petitioner had been implicated under different sections of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) the Prevention of Anti-Corruption Commission Act 1974 as stated above. 

 6. In paragraph 8 of the writ petition No. 7948 of 2009 it has been alleged that the FIR was lodged against the petitioner alleging an offence under different sections of the Penal Code and prevention of Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2004 giving rise to Motijheel Police Station Case No. 77 dated 28-12-2006. While both the cases were under investigation the petitioner moved this Division and obtained the present Rule and stay. 

 7. Mr. Abdul Matin Khoshru with Mr. Abdul Mannan, the learned Advocate after taking us with the writ petitions and Annexures with them mainly argued that both the FIR were lodged without prior sanction of the Anti-Corruption Commission in violation of the provision of section 32(1)(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act for which the initiation of both the cases i.e. Motijheel Police Station Case No. 77 and 79 have been made without lawful authority and without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect. 

 8. Mr. Md Khurshid Alam Khan and Mr. AKM Fazlul Hoque the learned counsel appearing for the respondents in the writ petitions commonly advanced the argument that the lodging of the FIR under different sections of the Penal Code and prevention of corruption Act against the petitioner is absolutely done in accordance with law and there is no violation of section 32(1)(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2004. In elaborating their arguments both the counsels brought to our notice that this issue has been finally set at rest by the Appellate Division in the Case of Anti-Corruption Commission, represented by its Chairman vs Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 wherein their Lordships of the Appellate Division unanimously observed that no sanction is required to file a complaint under the un-amended as well as amended section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2004. They further submit that their Lordships of the Appellate Division after examining the relevant laws and Rules in this respect came to such decision. 

 9. The learned counsel for the respondent also submits that right after lodging of the FIR when the investigation had just started the petitioner brought this writ petition which is also not tenable under law since no proceeding as such was pending before any competent Court of jurisdiction and for this reason interference by this Division at an initial stage of investigation cannot be supported under law. In this regard the decision of Abdul Hoque vs the State reported in 60 DLR (AD) 1 has been taken recourse to wherein their Lordships of the Appellate Division unanimously held that before taking of cognizance of a case by competent Court or tribunal a proceeding cannot be said to be pending an accordingly, a proceeding cannot be quashed unless cognizance in respect thereof has been taken and process issued. 

 10. We have heard the learned counsels for the petitioner and the respondents and considered their submissions. We have also gone through both the petitions and the different Annexures of the same and supplementary affidavits carefully. Since the decision of our apex Court clearly spelt out the provision of section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act in this context holding no sanction is required before filing a case under the Act and also on the point that a case cannot be quashed unless cognizance has been taken by the Court having jurisdiction we are of the view that both the points apply adversely in the instant writ petitions. 

 11. It has been argued that in violation of section 32(1)(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2004 the FIR was lodged against the petitioner since no sanction was obtained by the commission as required under the said provision. We hold that this question has been set at rest which is no longer a reintegrate. No sanction is required for lodging any FIR in contemplation with section 32(1)(2) of the Anti-Corruption Act 2004 un-amended or amended. This view reached in its finality in a very recent decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 wherein his Lordship Mr. Justice ABM Khairul Hoque while construing this point observed: 

 "The High Court Division, however, misinterpreted section 32 of the Act, the original as well as the amended one, in holding that a sanction by the commission is required before lodging an FIR. The high Court Division further misconceived the amended section 32 and wrongly held that a further sanction is required to take cognizance of the offence by the Court in spite of the sanction given earlier under sub-section (2) of Section 32 of the Act. But as a matter of fact no sanction is required to file a complaint and the unamended as well as the amended section 32 requires only one sanction from the Commission. 

 12. The second argument of the Learned Counsel for the respondent that right after lodging of the FIR when the investigation just had started the petitioner brought this writ petition which is not tenable under law since no proceeding as such was pending before any competent Court of jurisdiction also merits substance. In this regard the decision of Abdul Hoque vs State 60 DLR (AD) 1 as referred to above can profitably be cited wherein their Lordships of the Appellate Division after discussing pertinent portion of the reported cases of Bangladesh vs Tan Khong Hock 31 DLR (AD) 69, Syed Md Hashem vs State 48 DLR (AD) 87 and N Mahmud vs N Ahmed 36 DLR (AD) 14 unanimously held: 

 "All the cases seeking quashing of the proceeding were preferred before taking of cognizance of the offence by the senior Metropolitan Special Judge; ------ Accordingly, before taking of cognizance of a case by the competent court or tribunal a proceeding cannot be said to be pending and accordingly, a proceeding cannot be Quashed unless cognizance in respect thereof has been taken and process issued and so the instant criminal miscellaneous cases preferred under section 561A of the code of Criminal Procedure are Quite premature and so the high court Division should not enter into the first information report and the charge sheet in order to appreciate whether the facts alleged therein constitute any offence or not"
